title: Part time Bookkeeper
description:
Part Time Company Bookkeeper - Truro - £34,000 pro-rata

If you're an experienced Bookkeeper seeking part time hours with almost total flexibility over working patterns, this could be a great opportunity for you. Trial Balance Consulting have been assigned by a long established and highly successful services business based in Truro (with free onsite parking). The business operates a number of companies within its group, predominantly specialising in commercial services and development.

They currently seek to recruit a part time Company Bookkeeper to join their team. The role will work over 20 hours per week and offers a high degree of flexibility as to how and when these hours are completed; from two full working days to five part time working days, this employer is very happy to base working patterns around other commitments.

The business has implemented a move from SAGE to Xero accounting software and this is fully supported by the company's firm of Chartered Accountants. The successful candidate will ideally possess Xero experience, but exposure to another major cloud-based system who feel that they have the aptitude to adopt a new system are welcome to apply. The role calls for an experienced candidate with experience in all areas of SME bookkeeping to include sales/purchase ledger, bank reconciliations, VAT reporting and posting, payroll and CIS returns, monthly profit and loss and other management reports and other administration-based duties as required.

The role will form part of a small but very long standing and extremely friendly team, working from modern offices. For further details and to apply, please contact Steve Roach quoting reference SR11342.

title: Finance Assistant

title: O&M Administrator
description:
O & M Administrator

Construction - Renewables
Office based, occasional site visits, 40 hours per week.
£28,000pa Company bonus scheme
This is a permanent role working with a leading renewable energy contractor who's focus is servicing commercial properties.
They cover many areas around Devon and Cornwall and work away on projects further afield.
The O&M Administrator keeps our maintenance contracts running smoothly behind the scenes. You will schedule engineer visits, turn site inspection data into professional client reports, track faults and rectification work through to close-out, and keep contract, compliance and asset records accurate. You will be the first point of contact for O&M clients, freeing our engineers to focus on site work.

Benefits:
- £28,000pd.
- 22 days' holiday plus bank holidays.
- A small, friendly team doing work that matters for the energy transition.
- Casual dress, professional with a relaxed modern way of working.
- Company events.
- Workplace pension.
- Company bonus scheme

Job Spec/Key duties:
- Scheduling and planning
- Maintain the annual planned preventative maintenance (PPM) calendar across the O&M portfolio, so every visit, test and clean happens within contract.
- Book engineer visits, arrange site access, permits and inductions with clients (including NHS and university estates teams).
- Coordinate access equipment, subcontractors (e.g. panel cleaning, vegetation clearance) and materials for each visit.

Reporting
- Collate engineer inspection data, test sheets and photos, and check it is complete before the report is drafted.
- Produce client maintenance reports using ZLC templates, chasing engineers for missing results or evidence.
- Prepare monthly or quarterly performance summaries from monitoring platforms, flagging underperforming systems to the O&M Manager.
- Faults, rectification and reactive work
- Log client-reported and monitoring-alert faults, raise jobs and track them to resolution against contract response times.
- Maintain rectification schedules, request quotes, raise client approvals and follow up until works are complete.
- Manage warranty claims with manufacturers and distributors (inverters, modules, batteries).

Contract and commercial administration
- Keep O&M contract records up to date scope, visit frequency, service levels and renewal dates.
- Raise purchase orders and provide information for invoicing of planned and reactive work.
- Support the preparation of O&M proposals and tender returns with site data, references and pricing inputs.

Compliance and records
- Maintain asset registers for each site: system size, equipment, serial numbers, as-built drawings and O&M manuals.
- Track test due dates and certification (e.g. periodic inspection, IEC (phone number removed) testing), and keep evidence filed and retrievable.
- Ensure RAMS, permits and site safety documentation are issued and in date before each visit.
- Support the management team with audits, annual assessments and renewals across our accreditations: MCS (via NICEIC), ISO 9001, ISO 14001, RECC, Constructionline Gold, Cyber Essentials and B Corp.

Client communication
- Act as the day-to-day contact for O&M clients by phone and email, responding promptly and professionally.
- Keep clients informed of upcoming visits, findings and actions needed from them.

Required experience and skills:

Essential
- At least 2 years in an administration, coordination or scheduling role, ideally in a technical, construction, facilities or field-service business.
- Strong Microsoft 365 skills, especially Word, Excel and Outlook.
- Excellent written English and attention to detail you will be producing documents that go straight to clients.
- Highly organised, able to juggle many sites, deadlines and engineers at once.
- Confident, professional communicator by phone and email.

Desirable
- Experience in renewable energy, electrical contracting or building services O&M.
- Familiarity with solar PV monitoring portals.
- Experience with interpreting engineers inspection reports.
- Understanding of health and safety documentation (RAMS, permits to work, CDM).
- Experience working with public-sector clients such as the NHS or universities.
- Full UK driving licence.

Please apply or contact Ben Peel at Build Recruitment - South West on (phone number removed) for further details.

We'll take the time to understand your career history and motivations for a new role. We'll also take references and may ask for proof of eligibility to work in the UK.

We work with a wide variety of clients in the public and private sector, and we will work with you to identify clients in which your skills, experience and personality will fit. Once we submit you for a role you will receive support and regular communication throughout the interview process.

From there our commitment to you is all about being your career partner. We'll identify suitable jobs, provide support, and career guidance and even provide regular salary benchmarking.

title: Finance Assistant
description:
Finance Assistant (Temp-to-Perm)

Newquay Full-Time Immediate Start Available

Butler Rose is delighted to be working with a rapidly growing and ambitious organisation to recruit an Finance Assistant on a temp-to-perm basis. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced finance professional who is looking to secure a long-term position within a supportive and fast-paced business.

Joining a busy finance team, you will play a key role in delivering a robust finance service to the wider organisation, supporting senior stakeholders and helping to ensure the smooth day-to-day operation of the finance function. This position would suit someone who enjoys working across a broad range of finance responsibilities and takes pride in delivering high levels of accuracy and customer service.

Key Responsibilities
- Managing and monitoring the finance inbox, responding to queries and escalating issues where required.
- Administering the purchase order process, ensuring purchase orders are correctly matched to supplier invoices.
- Investigating and resolving purchase order discrepancies and supplier queries.
- Processing high volumes of supplier invoices accurately and efficiently onto the company's finance system.
- Preparing supplier payment runs and ensuring payments are made in line with agreed terms.
- Reconciling supplier statements and resolving outstanding balances.
- Acting as a key point of contact for supplier and customer finance-related queries.
- Setting up new suppliers and customers within the finance system.
- Performing bank reconciliations, including company credit card and expense account reconciliations.
- Supporting the monthly payroll process and pension administration.
- Managing employee expense claims and ensuring compliance with company procedures.
- Assisting with VAT preparation and submission activities.
- Supporting credit control processes, helping to ensure outstanding invoices are collected in a timely manner.
- Building strong working relationships across the business and providing finance support to non-financial stakeholders.

About You

The successful candidate is likely to have:
- Previous experience within an Accounts Assistant, Finance Assistant, Purchase Ledger or similar transactional finance role.
- Strong purchase ledger and reconciliation experience.
- Good working knowledge of accounting systems and Microsoft Excel.
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
- Strong communication skills and a professional approach when dealing with suppliers, customers and internal stakeholders.
- A high level of accuracy and attention to detail.
- A proactive and team-oriented attitude with a willingness to support wider finance activities.

What's on Offer?
- Temp-to-perm opportunity with genuine long-term prospects.
- Immediate start available.
- Varied and interesting finance role with exposure across multiple areas of accounting.
- Supportive and collaborative working environment.
- Opportunity to join a growing organisation during an exciting period of development.

If you're an experienced finance professional looking for your next opportunity in the Newquay area and are available to start at short notice, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Payroll Clerk
description:
The Opportunity

An established UK-based business is looking for a highly motivated, adaptable and organised Payroll & Timesheet Controller to join its Finance Team.

This is a newly created role offering the opportunity to take ownership of payroll administration and timesheet processes across the organisation.

Working closely with the Finance Manager, you will be responsible for ensuring accurate and efficient payroll processing, maintaining employee records and supporting the wider Finance and HR functions.

The successful candidate will be proactive, numerate and comfortable working to tight deadlines, with excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage their own workload.

Key Responsibilities
- Processing accurate weekly and monthly payroll.
- Taking ownership of the company-wide timesheet database, including subcontractors.
- Checking timesheets to ensure all information is complete and accurate.
- Chasing outstanding or late timesheet submissions.
- Processing weekly and monthly pension submissions and reconciling these against the accounts.
- Liaising with operational teams to ensure all working hours are accurately captured and reported.
- Working with department managers on payroll-related matters, including salary increases, new starters and banked hours/TOIL.
- Supporting the development and improvement of internal processes and procedures.
- Reviewing employee benefits, including Benefits in Kind (BIK), holiday entitlements and banked hours.
- Providing administrative support to HR and Finance, including preparation for annual audits.

About You

You will ideally have previous payroll and administration experience, with the confidence to manage a varied workload independently.

We're looking for someone who has:
- Strong numerical and organisational skills.
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
- The ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines.
- Good communication skills and the confidence to liaise with colleagues across different departments.
- A proactive approach and the ability to use initiative.
- Strong IT skills, particularly Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook.
- Experience using payroll software, ideally SAGE Payroll.

Desirable experience:
- Timesheet management.
- Pension administration.
- Benefits in Kind (BIK) and other HMRC payroll-related processes.

Salary & Benefits
- Salary of £28,000 - £32,000 per annum.
- Full-time hours, Monday to Friday, typically 9am-5pm.
- Some flexibility around working hours to suit workload requirements.
- 28 days annual leave, including bank holidays.
- Ongoing training and professional development opportunities.

Interested?

If you have payroll experience and are looking for an opportunity to take ownership of payroll and timesheet processes within an established business, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Administration Assistant
description: An exciting opportunity has arisen for a part time administration assistant working 30 hours a week within The Integrated Community Stroke Service (ICSS). ICSS provides specialist care for Stroke and Transient Ischaemic Attack (TIA) or mini stroke patients, their families and carers throughout Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly. The team consists of a Countywide Lead, Locality Team Leads, Stroke Specialist Nurses, Therapists, Business Support Supervisor, Secretaries and Administrative Assistants (this role). Under the direction of the Business Support Supervisor, this role will support the Integrated Community Stroke Service in administrative and secretarial duties, patient bookings and assisting with the input of clinical activity data. You should possess excellent communication, IT and time management skills to ensure the smooth running of the service. The role will be challenging and varied but ultimately a rewarding role that will provide an opportunity, for the right person, to become a key member of the team. Each team member is required to be flexible in contributing to the overall Trust agenda and in responding to changes in both management agenda and priorities. The post holder will be a key foundation member in providing full clerical support to various key functions within the ICSS Team to provide an efficient and effective administrative service. Be the first point of contact for all patients, their relatives, carers, health and social care professionals, referrers and visitors and ensure they are fully assisted, as required. To view a detailed job description and person specification including the main responsibilities of this role please see supporting documents.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: Job summary An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced, enthusiastic, motivated and hard-working individual to join our friendly and supportive team. You need to be flexible and be able to work in a fast-paced environment. Previous experience in General Practice would be advantage, although training will be provided. This will be for 30 hours per week, hours and days to be discussed at interview but to include Wednesday/Thursday evening until 8pm on a rota basis to cover annual leave and sickness. Please note, the post holder is required to work, on a rota basis, at our branch surgery in Rock, therefore a full driving licence and car is essential. Main Duties To provide an efficient and friendly service for all our patients and visitors, and to provide effective administrative support to our doctors and members of the clinical team. To be responsible for undertaking a wide range of reception duties and the provision of general support to the multidisciplinary team. Duties can include, but are not limited to, greeting and directing patients, effective use of the appointment system, booking appointments, the processing of information and assisting patients as required. To act as the central point of contact for patients, be responsible for the distribution of information, messages and enquiries for the clinical team, liaise with multi-disciplinary team members and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers. The following are the core responsibilities of the Receptionist. There may be, on occasion, a requirement to carry out other tasks. This will be dependent upon factors such as workload and staffing levels: Process personal, telephone and e-requests for appointments Answer incoming phone calls, transferring calls or dealing with the callers request appropriately Signpost patients to the correct service Initiating contact with and responding to, requests from patients, team members and external agencies Code data on the clinical IT system Photocopy documentation as required Data entry of new and temporary registrations and relevant patient information as required Input data into patients healthcare records as necessary Direct requests for information, i.e., SAR, insurance/solicitors letters and DVLA forms to the administrative team Manage all queries as necessary in an efficient manner Maintain a clean, tidy, effective working area at all times Monitor and maintain the reception area and notice boards Support all clinical staff with general tasks as requested In addition to the primary responsibilities, the Receptionist may be requested to: Action incoming emails and correspondence as necessary Scan patient related documentation and attach scanned documents to patients healthcare records Complete opening and closing procedures in accordance with the duty rota
